subject: Private deployment: key flow, BYO-key ops, and rotation plan for Acme
messages:
From: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@acme.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial KMS questions for private deployment

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. As we start to scope the private deployment (VPC) for Acme, the security team asked for a short write-up of the proposed key management approach. Two pressing points:

1) We need to confirm whether Redwood supports customer-provided keys (BYOK) with HSM-backed storage (we require FIPS 140-2 Level 3) and whether keys are ever exportable.
2) Rotation and emergency recovery: what are the suggested rotation cadences, tooling for automated rotation, and the playbook if a key is suspected compromised?

Can you share a short design and any diagrams or controls we should point to in our procurement checklist?

Best,
Emma
Emma Johnson
Security Architect, Acme Corp
attachment: acme_kms_requirements_v2.pdf (pdf)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: hiro.tanaka@redwood.com, mina.haddad@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial KMS questions for private deployment

Emma — thanks for the clear list. High level answers first, then a short ops-design and suggested next steps.

High level:
- BYOK + HSM: Yes — Redwood Private supports customer BYOK where the key material is generated and stored in a customer-managed HSM cluster (we integrate with AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM, and PKCS#11-compatible on-prem HSMs). We also provide an option to bring the key via encrypted import token to a Redwood-managed HSM in fully private deployments if customers request it.
- Exportability: Keys marked as HSM-protected are non-exportable by design. We only store key references and use envelope encryption for model data and tokenization.
- Rotation & recovery: We recommend a key rotation cadence of 90–180 days for data-encryption keys, and 12 months for root/KEK, depending on Acme policy. For emergency key compromise, there's a documented revocation + re-encryption path; I'll outline steps below.

Operations design (summary):
- Envelope encryption: Customer master key (CMK) in HSM protects per-instance data keys (DEKs). DEKs are rotated frequently and cached only in secure memory on inference nodes; they are never written to disk unencrypted.
- Key hierarchy: Root KEK (HSM, non-exportable) -> intermediate CMKs (HSM-wrapped) -> DEKs (short lived).
- Rotation: Automated orchestration via our Private control plane: new CMK version creation in HSM, rolling rewrap of DEKs, and staged re-encryption of long-lived artifacts (snapshots). We reuse a canary-first rollout to limit blast radius.
- Secrets handling: All service credentials stored in Vault (optional if customer has existing Vault; Redwood supports HashiCorp Vault, Azure Key Vault, and internal KMS). Transit operations use mTLS + signed requests; minimal IAM roles for key usage.
- Auditing & attestation: We log all KMS/HSM access calls to the customer-controlled audit sink (Syslog/S3) and surface per-key metrics in the Redwood Console.

I've attached a draft key-flow diagram and the procurement checklist edits. If that matches expectations, next step is to run a short tabletop with Acme SecOps and your procurement team this week.

Next steps proposed:
- Tabletop (technical + procurement) — Thu 2025-11-06, 10:00 PT
- Share a signed BYOK acceptance form and any ordering constraints (procurement)
- Identify a sandbox HSM we can use for end-to-end test

Thanks,
Dylan

Subject: HSM import and quotas
To: kiran.singh@cloudprovider.com

Hi all,
Quick points for the deployment:
- Bulk import of keys into CloudHSM requires a hardware-backed import token; token expiry is 72 hours. Plan for a single import window.
- Cross-region replication of HSM keys is not allowed for certain FIPS modes; recommend per-region keys and key wrapping for cross-region workloads.
- Soft deletion windows differ by provider; ensure your recovery playbook accounts for retention.

Regards,
Cloud HSM Services

Thanks — this is helpful. A few clarifying questions from our compliance team:

1) For backups and snapshots: If an inference node snapshot is taken for failover, are DEKs rewrapped with the latest CMK version automatically, or do you keep snapshots tied to the original key version? We need to understand the archival decryptability window.
2) Can Redwood support a split-knowledge / dual-control workflow for key import and rotation operations (our vendors require two approvers for key material operations)?
3) Will Redwood's audit logs include the HSM attestation certificate and the key version information for each access event?

Also, procurement will expedite the signed BYOK acceptance if you can provide the doc (we got a redline from legal for the standard bit).

Best,
Emma
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: hiro.tanaka@redwood.com, mina.haddad@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 15:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial KMS questions for private deployment

Emma — good questions; answers below plus a short mutual action plan.

1) Snapshots & archival decryptability:
- Snapshots are stored encrypted with the DEK that was current at snapshot time. During a scheduled maintenance rotation we rewrap existing DEKs with the new CMK version (rewrap = DEK encrypted under new KEK), which preserves snapshot decryptability without re-encrypting full snapshot payloads. For cold archives, we offer an optional archival re-encryption job that migrates older snapshots onto newer DEKs/CMKs if you want a single-key-window for long-term archives.

2) Split-knowledge / dual control:
- Yes. Our Private control plane supports a dual-approval flow for importing keys and promoting CMK versions. We can integrate with your approval system (SAML/OAuth) or run Vault-based approvers. The import window is gated: token generation requires two SRE approvers and the import operation requires a second approver. We will document the flow in the BYOK acceptance form.

3) Audit and attestation:
- Audit events include key_id, key_version, operation (encrypt/decrypt/sign), timestamp, and the HSM attestation certificate serial and fingerprint. We produce signed audit bundles and can push to your S3/Syslog; Redwood Console surfaces per-key access history as well.

Mutual action plan:
- Today: Share redlined BYOK acceptance form — procurement@redwood.com (we will also attach signed template).
- Thu 2025-11-13: Tabletop with Acme SecOps & Procurement (confirming: Thu 10:00 PT).
- Week of 2025-11-17: Sandbox import window and verification (single import token; Kiran and Cloud HSM will participate).

Attachments: signed-byoa-form.pdf (pending), INF-872 runbook (internal link)

Let us know if you want an expanded playbook for compromise recovery (we have a 1-page runbook we can share).

Thanks,
Dylan
